Subject: Hybrid endpoint SLA: time-to-first-token vs sustained tokens/sec — FinTech Solutions

Alex — attaching the draft SOW and a short SLA proposal for the hybrid endpoints we demoed last week. Procurement asked for explicit commitments around streaming vs non-streaming behavior, and we want to make sure the SOW language maps cleanly to your expectations. Key things we need you to confirm: 

- Time-to-first-token (TTFT) target for streaming endpoints and whether you need the metric measured per-request or as a percentile (P50/P95/P99).
- Sustained token/sec expectations for sustained conversational traffic vs one-off long-form generations (how do you want bursts handled).
- Whether you require a hard SLA (credit-backed) or an operational commitment during the pilot.

Proposed next steps: please review the attached SOW_FinTech_v1.pdf and the SLA_proposal_diff.docx and let us know whether procurement needs the new SLO table or a short addendum. If useful, we can run a short latency/payload test in your staging environment next week.

Attachments: SOW_FinTech_v1.pdf (SOW draft), SLA_proposal_diff.docx (differences compared to our standard SLA)

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechsolutions.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 13:22:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Hybrid endpoint SLA: time-to-first-token vs sustained tokens/sec — FinTech Solutions

Jordan — thanks for the materials. Quick answers from procurement and platform: 

- TTFT: For streaming endpoints we need a P95 TTFT of <200ms for end-user-facing paths. Measurement should be from request arrival at the edge to first byte emitted to the client. We understand pilot tolerance, but production procurement will require this as a stated SLO.
- Sustained throughput: For conversational workloads we expect a baseline of 120 tokens/sec sustained per endpoint with the ability to burst to 350 tokens/sec for up to 30 seconds for short user spikes. For long-form generations (>1,500 tokens) we prefer a separate class with negotiated throughput and an SLA carveout.
- Credits vs operational: Procurement wants credit-backed language for production in the final contract; pilot can be non-credit but must have clear monitoring and rollback policies.

Two notes: (1) We will need definitions and examples in the SOW for measurement (edge ingress times, time sync assumptions). (2) Security will request the SOC2 summary and audit logs retention details before signing.

Attached: procurement_note_1126.pdf (short summary for legal)

Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
FinTech Solutions

Subject: Re: Hybrid endpoint SLA: time-to-first-token vs sustained tokens/sec — FinTech Solutions

Alex — appreciate the clear guidance. I pulled together the baseline options that map to your asks and a set of carveouts we usually add for long-form workloads. Summary below (we can move any of this into an SOW table or an addendum):

Option A — Production SLA (credit-backed)
- Streaming TTFT: P95 < 200ms measured edge-to-first-byte.
- Sustained throughput: 120 tokens/sec baseline per endpoint; burst to 350 tokens/sec for up to 30s.
- Long-form generation (>1,500 tokens): different performance class; negotiated throughput and separate SLOs (no burst guarantee).

Option B — Pilot (operational commitments, non-credit)
- Streaming TTFT: P95 < 250ms (pilot tolerance), with rollout to 200ms on production cutover.
- Sustained throughput: baseline 100 tokens/sec, burst to 300 tokens/sec during pilot windows.
- Canary rollout: staged traffic (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on error/latency regressions.

Carveouts we propose to include in the SOW text:
- Measurement clarity: TTFT defined as edge-received timestamp to first byte emitted; percentiles computed over 24h windows.
- Burst policy: bursts are measured at endpoint level; sustained guarantees exclude sustained continuous loads over 10 minutes without pre-notification.
- Fallback behavior: for very long generations, Redwood can route to a non-streaming batch path with documented timings and customer notification; this path will not count as a SLA breach if pre-negotiated.
- Force majeure and cloud-provider-induced network events will be exempted per standard addendum.

Actions for us: Marissa/legal, can you review the credit wording and the force majeure carveout? Karthik, can you confirm we can meet the measurement definitions from our telemetry and that we can instrument a 24h P95 report for the pilot?

I attached an "SLA_matrix.xlsx" that lays out the three columns (Pilot | Production standard | Long-form generation) with the numbers above. If this mapping looks right I can prepare a short addendum to the SOW and a pilot runbook for their staging environment next week.

Thanks — Jordan

Alex / Jordan — looping in with redlines and our legal/ops positions. We are comfortable agreeing to the production numbers in Option A with the following contract language and monitoring commitments: 

1) Definitions and measurement
- TTFT: measured at edge ingress to first byte emitted to client; telemetry will report P50/P95/P99 over rolling 24h windows.
- Sustained throughput: tokens/sec measured as an average over 60s windows; bursts defined as sustained >baseline for less than 30s.

2) Pilot-to-Prod transition
- Pilot period: 30 days of operational verification. Production SLA and credit terms become effective after a successful acceptance test and a signed SOW addendum.

3) Carveouts and exceptions
- Long-form generation (>1,500 tokens) will be scoped to a separate SLO; Redwood will notify FinTech Solutions at least 48h in advance for any planned routing of long-form traffic to a non-streaming path.
- Force majeure & provider network events as standard exclusions.

4) Monitoring and evidence
- Redwood will provide an automated daily P95 TTFT report and a token/sec dashboard link with 90-day retention for the pilot; production will extend to 365-day retention as an add-on.

5) Credits
- If P95 TTFT > 200ms for more than two 24h windows in a 30-day period, FinTech Solutions will be eligible for service credits equal to 5% of monthly fees for each additional failure window, up to 25% per month.

If that looks acceptable we will prepare the SOW addendum and send it to procurement/legal for signature. Two asks for FinTech: (a) confirm that the 30-day pilot period is acceptable, and (b) confirm whether your security team still needs a SOC2 summary or the full report before signature.

Best,
Marissa Cole
